statement: A valid XES/OCEL document is not proof that its events, objects, qualifiers or attributes have the intended domain meaning.
An object identity or type is not an inherent process case; a case is a declared projection with loss.
Timestamp or directly-follows order does not by itself establish causal influence.
An object-object relation without temporal semantics cannot represent every dynamic relationship unambiguously.
A changed attribute becomes a state transition only under a declared domain state function and leading-object perspective.
A generated state-transition event or aggregate process event must retain derivation provenance and cannot rewrite the source log.
OCEL is an exchange format within the broader OCED design space; conventions and extensions remain explicit.
Object-centric event-data semantics and an event-knowledge-graph analytical projection have different identities and compatibility rules.
An EKG without temporal entity-snapshot semantics is not equivalent to a tEKG.
A discovered model is a method/configuration-scoped finding, not the authoritative intended process.
Conformance fitness or an alignment does not alone prove legal, policy or control compliance.
Token replay and optimal alignment have different completeness, optimality and resource contracts.
A measured queue or delay concentration is a bottleneck candidate, not a causal diagnosis.
No process-mining result may authorize a mutation, accuse a person or waive a control without an external decision authority.
Two equal projected traces or graphs need not preserve equal source histories, objects or relations.
The same event can carry different state-aware meanings for different leading objects.
Absence in an admitted event cut cannot prove that no world event occurred.
JSON, XML, SQLite and other carriers are equivalent only under an explicit semantic round-trip and loss profile.
